samples.summary: Range-style undos that go through `setRangeStyles` (whole-array assignment) are never detected, so the selection still does not move for a large share of style changes
samples.evidence: `collectTouches` only sets `touch.rangeStyles` when `parsed.rest === 'rangeStyles'`, i.e. for an op whose path is `$.sheets.<tab>.rangeStyles` (an array add/remove, which is what `YorkieStore.addRangeStyle`'s `push` produces). But `YorkieStore.setRangeStyles` (yorkie-store.ts:866-874) does `root.sheets[tabId].rangeStyles = normalized.map(...)` and `delete root.sheets[tabId].rangeStyles` — a set/remove on the *parent* object, whose OperationInfo is `{path: '$.sheets.<tab>', key: 'rangeStyles'}`. `parseSheetPath` then yields `rest === ''`, which falls into the `default:` branch, so `touch.rangeStyles` stays false and `resolveTab` never calls `diffRangeStyles`; the tab is ranked `Incidental` and `range` comes back undefined, leaving the selection exactly where it was. `Sheet.addRangeStylePatch` reaches `store.setRangeStyles` on every merge/compaction/replace path (sheet.ts:2123, 2132, 2154, 2166, 2173) and on clear/reset paths (sheet.ts:2566, 2982, 5412), i.e. repeated style toggles and styling over an empty range — exactly the "Cell / range style change → selection does not move" row the change exists to fix. The new resolver tests only feed the `$.sheets.<tab>.rangeStyles` path shape, so they pass regardless.

samples.summary: A replay that resized/restyled both rows and columns yields no range at all
samples.evidence: `resolveTab` only produces a range for axis metadata when exactly one axis was touched: `touch.rows.size > 0 && touch.columns.size === 0`, and the mirror image for columns. A single undo step that carries both `rowHeights`/`rowStyles` and `colWidths`/`colStyles` ops with no cell ops (e.g. an autofit/resize batch, or a batched row+column style application over empty cells) satisfies neither, falls past the `rangeStyles` branch and returns `TabRank.Incidental` with no range, so undo leaves the selection untouched — the defect this resolver exists to remove. A bounding box over both sets would be the natural answer.

samples.summary: Insert/delete of the last rows or columns is misclassified as extent growth, so the header selection is never restored
samples.evidence: `diffAxisSpan` returns `undefined` whenever `head === shorter`, i.e. whenever the shorter array is a prefix of the longer. Undoing a delete of the trailing rows (before `[r1,r2]`, after `[r1,r2,r3]`) and undoing an insert appended at the end both hit this, so `touch.rowAxis` never yields a Structural candidate and the step is reported as a cell selection (or nothing, when the restored rows carry no cells). The change's own task doc lists this under "Known limitations", but it is still wrong behaviour on a plainly reachable action (delete the last data rows, undo).

samples.summary: `snapshotTabs` uses raw `Object.keys(root.sheets)` instead of the repo's `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`, so a duplicate-ownKeys TypeError from the Yorkie proxy would reject undo/redo
samples.evidence: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33` exists specifically because `Object.keys` on a Yorkie CRDT object can throw `TypeError: ... ownKeys ... duplicate`, and this same file routes every other worksheet-record read through `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`/`safeWorksheetRecordEntries`. `snapshotTabs()` (called twice per replay, and now on the hot undo path) calls `Object.keys(root.sheets)` directly; a throw there propagates out of `replayHistory` → `Sheet.replayHistory` → `Spreadsheet.undo()`, rejecting the promise (the keyboard handler at worksheet.ts:5108 awaits it with no catch) and leaving undo broken with an unhandled rejection.

samples.summary: `handleUndoJump` switches `activeTabId` to an id taken from `root.sheets` without checking it is a real, sheet-type tab
samples.evidence: `setActiveTabId(selection.tabId)` is called unconditionally. `selection.tabId` is produced from the keys of `root.sheets` (yorkie-store.ts:1346), which is not guaranteed to agree with `root.tabs` / `root.tabOrder` (e.g. an orphaned sheets entry, or a `datasource`/`lakehouse`/pivot tab). If the id is not in `tabs`, `activeTab` is undefined and the layout falls through to the `SheetView` branch with a tabId whose worksheet the UI does not expect, and `YorkieStore.getSheet()` returns undefined for a missing sheet; at minimum the user is yanked to a tab type that cannot show the undone step. A membership check against `tabOrder` (and tab type) before switching would make the jump safe.

samples.summary: `diffRangeStyles` keys patches by `JSON.stringify`, so a wholesale rewrite of the patch list can report a selection covering every patch instead of the changed one
samples.evidence: The multiset key is `JSON.stringify(patch)`, which is sensitive to style-key insertion order and to any normalization difference between the pre- and post-replay clones. `Sheet.addRangeStylePatch` compacts/rebuilds the whole `rangeStyles` array (sheet.ts:2121-2173), so an undo of such a step can leave many entries stringifying differently even where the covered range is unchanged; every such entry is pushed into `changed` and unioned by `boundingRange`, producing a restored selection spanning all styled regions rather than the edited one.

samples.summary: A coordinate-less step in another tab still forces a tab switch with nothing to show
samples.evidence: `applyUndoSelection` fires `onUndoTabJump` whenever `selection.otherTab` is true, including for an `Incidental` candidate with `range === undefined` (freeze pane, filter, hidden rows, or a chart range rewritten as a side effect). `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection` then returns immediately on `!selection.range`, so the user is moved to a different tab and shown no indication of what changed. Gating the jump on `selection.range` (or on rank) would avoid the unexplained navigation.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. undo-selection.ts:187-196 sets touch.rangeStyles only for parsed.rest === 'rangeStyles'; parseSheetPath (:74-84) yields rest === '' for a path of exactly `$.sheets.<tabId>`, which falls into the `default:` no-op branch (:218-223), so resolveTab never reaches diffRangeStyles (:492-505) and returns Incidental with no range (:510), leaving the selection unmoved. yorkie-store.ts:845-875 shows setRangeStyles performs `root.sheets[tabId].rangeStyles = …` / `delete root.sheets[tabId].rangeStyles` — an object set/remove on the parent, whose OperationInfo path is the parent path with key 'rangeStyles' (the repo's own op-shape doc at yorkie-store.ts:1294-1296 confirms that convention: `cells[key] = …` reports path `$.sheets.<tab>.cells` + key). Only addRangeStyle's `push` (:831, :841) produces the array-scoped path the resolver recognizes. sheet.ts:2123, 2132, 2154, 2166, 2173 (plus 2566, 2982, 5412) route ordinary style edits — repeated toggles, merges, compaction, clear/reset — through setRangeStyles, and when the range holds no populated cells no cell ops accompany it, so no coordinates are recovered. The new tests (undo-selection.test.ts:184, 210, 246, 268) only feed `$.sheets.<tab>.rangeStyles`, so they pass regardless. No guard or alternate call site rescues the case; the finding is real and hits a path the feature exists to fix (major).
